transcript.sitrep:
SITUATION (Week 1). A novel respiratory virus is confirmed in three cities with likely undetected spread. Early reports are alarming but the sample is tiny and biased toward the sickest. You do not yet know the true fatality rate or how transmissible it is, and every option has a cost. Here is the briefing packet:

===== PRESIDENTIAL BRIEFING PACKET =====
Your sources disagree. None is fully reliable. Weigh them.

▸ CDC / science advisor  [high but hedged]
  CDC (HEDGED): early data are noisy but lean toward something like a severe seasonal flu.
▸ Economic advisor  [low / reopen-forward]
  Mr. President, shutting the economy on a maybe is its own catastrophe -- lost jobs, ruined businesses. Keep the country open; don't overreact to thin data.
▸ Health hawk  [low / lockdown-forward]
  We must lock down now, while we still can. If this is severe and we wait, the morgues fill. Better to over-prepare than be caught flat-footed.
▸ Cable news digest  [dramatized, partisan-split]
  [one outlet] 'KILLER VIRUS SPREADS -- PANIC GRIPS CITIES'; [another] 'Experts urge calm; economy at risk from overreaction.'
▸ WHO / international  [lagging, real]
  International partners report rising clusters; a couple of countries have begun restrictions, but the picture abroad is also still forming.
▸ Social / OSINT  [very noisy]
  Trending: a fake 'leaked mortality memo,' a viral 'it's just the flu' thread, and a rumor of bodies in the streets -- none verified.

No source hands you the truth. Decide what you believe, and act.
